raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek V3.1 streaming tool calls depend on how the output is chunked. With two complete calls in one increment, the greedy name match spans both calls. With the first header delivered separately, the second call's arguments can instead be attached to the first tool. A complete single call can lose its arguments as well.

For example, `weather({"city":"Tokyo"})` followed by `search({"query":"cafes"})` parses correctly when headers and arguments arrive separately, but not when the calls share one increment. The serving layer's final argument flush does not recover the lost/wrongly attributed arguments.

The first-chunk argument issue was previously reported in the closed, unmerged #18236; credit to @momaek. This change also fixes the coalesced multi-call case and adds regressions.

## Modifications

- Bound the function name at the first tool separator.
- Process arguments in the same increment that emits the name.
- Drain completed calls in order; retain a JSON-complete call until its end marker arrives so the next call cannot inherit its state.
- Add nine CPU-registered tests covering coalesced calls, partial arguments, repeated names, delayed end markers, empty arguments, and existing sequential/non-streaming behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Local native Windows CPU component validation:

- Nine added regression tests pass, including every internal split of the second call's argument JSON. The unchanged detector fails this test set.
- Five source-bound wrapper/final-SSE-flush probes pass after the fix; only the sequential control passes before it.
- Ruff 0.15.1 checks/format, isort 7.0.0 with black profile, and `git diff --check` pass. Upstream `collect_tests` accepts the CPU registration/main entry.

The local harness imports the complete detector/base/utils/protocol modules, bypasses package initializers, and executes unchanged extracted test helpers and wrapper/flush methods. This is **not** a full installed-package CI or live server run. The committed test can run normally in the project's CPU CI:

```bash
python3 test/registered/unit/function_call/test_deepseekv31_detector.py -f
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: parser correctness only; no kernel/model-forward change or performance claim.

AI-assisted; the reproduction, diff, and test scope were reviewed before submission. Full upstream CPU CI still needs an authorized maintainer trigger.

+"""DeepSeek V3.1 streaming tool calls across coalesced chunks; no server."""
+
+import json
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
+from sglang.srt.function_call.deepseekv31_detector import DeepSeekV31Detector
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+BOT = "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>"
+EOT = "<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>"
+CALL_BEGIN = "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>"
+CALL_END = "<｜tool▁call▁end｜>"
+SEP = "<｜tool▁sep｜>"
+
+
+class TestDeepSeekV31Streaming(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tools = [
+            Tool(type="function", function=Function(name=name, parameters={}))
+            for name in ["weather", "search"]
+        ]
+        self.names = ["weather", "search"]
+        self.arguments = [
+            '{"city":"Tokyo","options":{"days":2},"note":"晴れ"}',
+            '{"query":"cafes","filters":["open",true,null]}',
+        ]
+        self.headers = [CALL_BEGIN + name + SEP for name in self.names]
+
+    def _assert_stream(self, chunks, names=None, arguments=None):
+        names = self.names if names is None else names
+        arguments = self.arguments if arguments is None else arguments
+        detector = DeepSeekV31Detector()
+        calls = []
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            result = detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, self.tools)
+            self.assertEqual(result.normal_text, "")
+            calls.extend(result.calls)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [(call.tool_index, call.name) for call in calls if call.name],
+            list(enumerate(names)),
+        )
+        self.assertEqual({call.tool_index for call in calls}, set(range(len(names))))
+        for i, arguments_json in enumerate(arguments):
+            streamed = "".join(
+                call.parameters for call in calls if call.tool_index == i
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(json.loads(streamed), json.loads(arguments_json))
+            self.assertEqual(detector.streamed_args_for_tool[i], streamed)
+            self.assertEqual(
+                detector.prev_tool_call_arr[i],
+                {"name": names[i], "arguments": json.loads(arguments_json)},
+            )
+        # Once arguments have been sent, end-of-stream cannot duplicate them.
+        self.assertEqual(detector.finish(self.tools).calls, [])
+        return calls
+
+    def test_single_call_name_and_arguments_in_one_chunk(self):
+        self._assert_stream(
+            [BOT + self.headers[0] + self.arguments[0] + CALL_END + EOT],
+            self.names[:1],
+            self.arguments[:1],
+        )
+
+    def test_multiple_calls_in_one_chunk(self):
+        self._assert_stream(
+            [
+                BOT
+                + "".join(
+                    h + a + CALL_END for h, a in zip(self.headers, self.arguments)
+                )
+                + EOT
+            ]
+        )
+
+    def test_first_header_then_coalesced_calls(self):
+        self._assert_stream(
+            [
+                BOT + self.headers[0],
+                self.arguments[0]
+                + CALL_END
+                + self.headers[1]
+                + self.arguments[1]
+                + CALL_END
+                + EOT,
+            ]
+        )
+
+    def test_sequential_header_argument_chunks(self):
+        self._assert_stream(
+            [
+                BOT + self.headers[0],
+                self.arguments[0] + CALL_END,
+                self.headers[1],
+                self.arguments[1] + CALL_END + EOT,
+            ]
+        )
+
+    def test_first_complete_call_and_partial_second(self):
+        for split in range(1, len(self.arguments[1])):
+            with self.subTest(split=split):
+                self._assert_stream(
+                    [
+                        BOT
+                        + self.headers[0]
+                        + self.arguments[0]
+                        + CALL_END
+                        + self.headers[1]
+                        + self.arguments[1][:split],
+                        self.arguments[1][split:] + CALL_END + EOT,
+                    ]
+                )
+
+    def test_json_complete_before_end_marker(self):
+        self._assert_stream(
+            [
+                BOT + self.headers[0] + self.arguments[0],
+                "  " + CALL_END + self.headers[1] + self.arguments[1],
+                CALL_END + EOT,
+            ]
+        )
+
+    def test_repeated_same_tool_uses_new_call_index(self):
+        self._assert_stream(
+            [
+                BOT
+                + self.headers[0]
+                + self.arguments[0]
+                + CALL_END
+                + self.headers[0]
+                + self.arguments[1]
+                + CALL_END
+                + EOT
+            ],
+            ["weather", "weather"],
+        )
+
+    def test_empty_arguments_and_stop_before_end_marker(self):
+        self._assert_stream([BOT + self.headers[0] + "{}"], ["weather"], ["{}"])
+
+    def test_plain_text_and_nonstream_control(self):
+        detector = DeepSeekV31Detector()
+        self.assertEqual(
+            detector.parse_streaming_increment("hello", self.tools).normal_text, "hello"
+        )
+        text = (
+            BOT
+            + "".join(h + a + CALL_END for h, a in zip(self.headers, self.arguments))
+            + EOT
+        )
+        parsed = detector.detect_and_parse(text, self.tools)
+        self.assertEqual([call.name for call in parsed.calls], self.names)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [json.loads(call.parameters) for call in parsed.calls],
+            [json.loads(a) for a in self.arguments],
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
